title: Musk says Nvidia will lose 'critical' deals without Jensen Huang
author: Xebec
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Elon Musk has warned that Nvidia could lose critical business deals without Jensen Huang, arguing that some relationships depend on personal trust in the ousted chief executive. Reuters reported on November 14 that Musk praised Huang’s management of Nvidia’s supply chain and said many arrangements rested on personal agreements rather than written contracts.

The report does not identify the deals, name the counterparties or establish that any agreement has been cancelled. Musk’s comments should therefore be understood as a warning about potential disruption, rather than evidence that Nvidia has already lost business.

The broader issue is how much of a company’s competitive strength belongs to its institutions and how much depends on one individual. If Musk’s assessment is accurate, Nvidia faces a challenge extending beyond appointing a successor: it must preserve relationships that may have been built around Huang personally.

For a chip supplier, dependable commercial relationships can influence production planning, delivery schedules and customers’ confidence. If partners reconsider informal commitments during a leadership transition, uncertainty could spread through purchasing decisions and investment plans. Those are possible consequences, however, not outcomes demonstrated by the Reuters report.

The warning also puts succession planning under scrutiny. A durable business needs teams, documented commitments and clear decision processes that allow important relationships to survive executive departures. Personal trust can help secure agreements quickly, but reliance on it can make a transition harder to manage.

For customers and investors, the question is whether Nvidia can demonstrate continuity. Evidence would include partners reaffirming commitments, deliveries proceeding as expected and management clarifying responsibility for major relationships.

Bottom line: It is nice to see that Musk has Jensen's back here but Musk’s intervention highlights a common business risk rather than proving an immediate crisis. Nvidia’s test is whether the confidence associated with Huang can transfer to the organization, keeping partnerships stable as leadership changes and counterparties reassess their commitments. As an insider I can tell you that the risk is minimal. Nvidia is much more than just Jensen. However, I wouldn't be surprised to see Jensen come back as CEO emeritus or something like that, absolutely.
